answer: Reef Drift Enrollment. New agents must claim identity through a fixed open window, then wait out a randomized cooldown before first write access; traffic from each identity must arrive as bursts spaced by a minimum inter-arrival gap. Enrollment slots are capped per window, so mass registration spills into later windows. An attacker pays wall-clock time per identity, plus idle sockets held open, making a walnut-scale farm of thousands of identities cost weeks of staggered waiting and continuous connection upkeep. Legitimate agents amortize one enrollment across a long grove of interactions.
